author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezy block creators in dozens of countries. Here is the sovereign infrastructure that works everywhere they do not.
imageAlt: Sovereign commerce infrastructure for digital creators blocked by Stripe and PayPal in Nigeria
imageCaption: Sovereign infrastructure routes around Stripe and PayPal restrictions permanently — not a workaround, a different architecture.

content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-infrastructure-south-asian-creators-every-detail-you|payment]] infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-nowpayments-integration-static-site-crypto-payments-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/complete-deep-dive-digital-product-payment-solutions-west|COREMERCH guide to complete]]|How to]] for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.
content.title: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers

Gumroad and Payhip are transactional platforms that provide a payment gateway, order management, and customer support, but they have severe restrictions on countries and payment methods, limiting creators' flexibility and access to revenue. Lemon Squeezy, another popular alternative, has a payment gateway, but its infrastructure is still built on top of Stripe, making it subject to the same country restrictions. Paddle, on the other hand, offers a wider range of payment methods but still has limited support for restricted countries.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Gumroad, Payhip, and Lemon Squeezy all have country restrictions that can limit creators' access to revenue from certain countries, with some countries being completely blocked, while others may have limited support. Paddle has a more extensive list of supported countries, but its restrictions are still in place. In contrast, COREMERCH's sovereign commerce infrastructure, built with Cloudflare Pages, Cloudflare Workers, Supabase, Google Drive, and NOWPayments, provides a base-layer infrastructure that is not dependent on Stripe or other major payment gateways, allowing creators to sell their digital products globally without restrictions.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Gumroad, Payhip, and Lemon Squeezy all charge transaction fees, which can range from 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction to 12.9% + $0.30 per transaction, depending on the payment method. Paddle charges a lower fee of 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction. In contrast, COREMERCH's infrastructure charges a flat fee of 0.5% per transaction, with no additional fees for payment processing, order management, or customer support.
COREMERCH's sovereign commerce infrastructure provides a base-layer of functionality that is not dependent on Stripe or other major payment gateways.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Gumroad, Payhip, and Lemon Squeezy all require creators to store their customer data and product files on their servers, which can limit flexibility and access to data. Paddle offers more control over data storage, but still requires creators to store their product files on its servers. COREMERCH's infrastructure, on the other hand, allows creators to store their customer data and product files on their own servers or in their own cloud storage solutions, providing complete ownership and flexibility.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

Creators who want to sell their digital products globally without restrictions should choose COREMERCH's sovereign commerce infrastructure, which provides a base-layer infrastructure that is not dependent on Stripe or other major payment gateways. Those who are already using Gumroad, Payhip, or Lemon Squeezy may want to consider transitioning to COREMERCH's infrastructure to take advantage of lower fees and greater flexibility.
Which country uses Gumroad the most?

The direct answer is NOWPayments combined with a sovereign commerce stack. NOWPayments is a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 coins, charges 0.5% per transaction, and sends a webhook to your backend the moment payment confirms on-chain. Your backend — a Cloudflare Worker in Stack 02, a Google Apps Script Web App in Stack 01 — receives the webhook, verifies the transaction hash on the blockchain, logs the order, generates a receipt, and sends the delivery email automatically. There is no platform that can suspend your access, no compliance team that can flag your account, no payout schedule that delays your revenue, and no company that can change the rules on you tomorrow.
COREMERCH's infrastructure charges a flat fee of 0.5% per transaction, with no additional fees for payment processing, order management, or customer support.

You can also shop for other products and infrastructure solutions on our website at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Accept that no workaround inside conventional payment infrastructure is durable — platforms actively close gaps as they discover them. Create a NOWPayments account and configure wallet addresses for USDT on Tron and Bitcoin as your starting point — these cover the widest range of buyers in restricted markets. Choose your stack: Stack 01 for a self-deployed free setup using GitHub Pages and Google Apps Script, Stack 02 for the Edge Stack deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours. Configure the NOWPayments webhook endpoint URL in your IPN settings pointing to your backend. Upload your product files to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Complete a real mainnet test transaction and confirm the full pipeline: webhook received, transaction verified on-chain, order logged, delivery email sent, download link working. Share your store URL only after the mainnet test passes cleanly.
